subtype: Approach: reversible trial before a full move [Action]
passage:
I work two desks from Abhinav, and this spring I watched Abhinav decide about moving abroad. Everyone expected an announcement, a farewell cake. Instead, Abhinav knocked on the manager's door one Monday and asked for a three-month stint at our partner office overseas.
"I want to see it first," Abhinav told me at the coffee machine. "Resigning is a one-way door."
Abhinav left in April. Photos arrived: a small flat, a rainy commute. In July Abhinav came back, tanned and quieter, and told us, "Good, but not settled yet." I can't tell whether that was relief or disappointment, and Abhinav has not said.
— Jaya

qa.a: Abhinav was probably cautious and hopeful, wanting to see it first, since resigning is a one-way door.

qa.q: What could Abhinav do now to decide whether to make the move permanent?
qa.a: Abhinav could list what felt good and hard in the three months and compare it with what matters most before choosing.

qa.a: Jaya is curious and a little unsure, unable to tell whether Abhinav's quiet return was relief or disappointment.

subtype: Approach: reversible trial before a full move [Action]
passage:
August. Kunal almost sent his resignation to join a Berlin startup. Instead he asked his manager, Anirban, for fifteen minutes. 'Is there any project where I could work from our Amsterdam office for a few months?' Anirban said he'd check.
October. Kunal landed in Amsterdam on a four-month assignment, same salary, his flat in Pune still rented and his return ticket booked. He cooked dal in a shared kitchen, cycled in the rain and called home more often than he expected.
February, back in Pune. He sat with Anirban again. 'The work was great. The dark by half past four and eating alone most nights, I didn't love that.' He hadn't decided yet. But now he was deciding with four months of real life behind him, not a dream.

qa.q: How long was Kunal's assignment in Amsterdam?
How does Kunal seem to feel in February about life abroad?
qa.a: Kunal feels mixed: he enjoyed the work but felt lonely eating alone and low in the early dark.

qa.q: What could Kunal try next before a permanent decision?
qa.a: He could ask about a remote arrangement or a second assignment in a lighter season, to see whether the loneliness eases with time.

qa.q: How might Anirban see Kunal's request in August?
qa.a: Anirban got a chance to keep a good engineer by offering a trial instead of losing him to a resignation.

grounding: It shows a young man asking his employer for a short overseas assignment instead of resigning, to learn how life abroad feels before committing.

subtype: Approach: reversible trial before a full move [Action]
passage: Hafsa, before you resign, let your Shankar sir tell you something. When I was twenty-six in the Chennai office, I wanted London more than anything. Everyone said, quit, go, don't look back. Instead I asked my boss for a six-month posting there. He looked surprised, but he agreed. I kept my room at home and told my mother it was a trial. Those six months taught me what no brochure could: I loved the work, but I hated the long commute, and I missed my mother's Sunday phone calls more than I expected. When I came back, I didn't move for good. I took a role with more foreign travel instead. Two weeks abroad, then home. It fit me. If I had resigned first, I'd have learnt all this with no job to come back to.

qa.q: How long was Shankar's posting in London?
How did Shankar feel during those six months?
qa.a: He loved the work but felt worn down by the commute and homesick for his mother's Sunday calls.

qa.q: What was the key choice in Shankar's story, and why did it help?
qa.a: Asking his boss for a posting instead of resigning, because he could learn how life abroad felt and still come back to a job.

qa.q: How might Shankar's mother have felt about the trial?
qa.a: Knowing it was a trial, she may have felt less fearful of losing him, and relieved when he chose a role that brought him home often.

grounding: It shows a young man asking his employer for a short overseas posting instead of resigning, to learn how life abroad feels before committing.
